overview: Dubai and Abu Dhabi pack theme parks, aquariums, desert safaris and the world's tallest building into a 4-hour flight. Very safe, spotless, with plenty of Indian food.
fit: Superb for both kids in the cooler months.
season: November to March is pleasant (18–30°C). April–October is very hot (40°C+). Dubai Shopping Festival runs Dec–Jan.

gettingThere.detail: Chennai to Dubai direct (Emirates, IndiGo, Air India Express)

gettingAround: Dubai Metro and taxis; a car with driver for Abu Dhabi.

todo.title: Burj Khalifa At the Top and Dubai Fountain
todo.why: Views and the free fountain show

todo.title: Desert safari
todo.book: Ask for gentle driving with small kids

todo.title: Ferrari World or Warner Bros. World, Abu Dhabi

stay.why: Indian food, near metro, good value
Near Burj Khalifa and the mall

save: Buy park combos (Yas Island multi-park passes)
Stay in Bur Dubai and use the metro
safety: Very safe; respect local laws and dress codes in religious places
kids: Plan one big park per day max
Evening fountain shows are free and magical

days.plan: Abu Dhabi: Grand Mosque and Ferrari World

visa: Indian passport holders need a UAE tourist visa before travel, applied through the airline (Emirates/IndiGo/Air India) or an agent; usually 2–4 days, ~₹7,000–8,000 per person for 30 days. Indians with a valid US visa/green card or UK/EU residence can get visa on arrival.
